$comment: Architecture evidence for the two leading contrasting operating models. Counts exclude blank lines and comments. Change drills record the propagation mechanism already exercised by the paired builds; they do not claim elapsed implementation time.
capability: Realistic records workspace: filters, faceting, sorting, selection, pagination, locale-aware formatting and result announcements

ownership.hostResidue: frame, page composition, Delta-only wizard/menu, and host reset repair

token.evidence: Shipped CSS retains var(--undrr-*) references; a token stylesheet swap reaches both consumers.

interactionPolicy.evidence: Filtering, reset-to-first-page, settled announcements, sorting and pagination now have one implementation imported by both hosts.

rtlAndLocalisation.evidence: Both consumers pass the locale through one shared context; logical CSS and React Aria locale behaviour handle direction.

react-aria.visualAuthorityNote: The shared records layer owns layout and consumes UNDRR custom properties directly. Host-specific theme files still repair each host reset, so the experiment proves a shared product layer, not zero host adaptation.

ownership.componentAppearance: shared MUI theme plus per-host repair
ownership.hostResidue: host frame, stylesheet order and 11-27 lines of host repair CSS

token.evidence: The shared theme centralises mapping, but token values are resolved into bundle output rather than remaining live custom-property references.

interactionPolicy.evidence: Both hosts import the same integration package; a shared component or default changes once and is rebuilt into each site.

rtlAndLocalisation.evidence: Shared configuration cannot flip physical offsets already emitted by Emotion; the documented remedy adds a third-party RTL transform forbidden by the evaluation.

mui.visualAuthorityNote: UNDRR can centralise a theme and wrappers, but MUI retains component structure, state semantics and physical-layout choices; host repair remains per site.
